clips.title: About DRAFT Pull Requests
clips.why: The whole idea of a draft PR in under a minute and a half: open the PR early, but say it is not ready.
look: A draft cannot be merged until someone marks it ready for review.
Opening early is still useful: CI runs and the work is visible.
clips.after: Every agent PR starts this way, and only the ready gate is allowed to press the button you see here.

clips.title: GitHub branch rules (protect your git branches)
clips.why: How a branch demands a pull request, an approval and green checks before anything can be merged.
look: "Require a pull request before merging" with a number of approvals: our main ruleset asks for exactly one.
Required status checks: the checks named here are the ones gh pr checks --required lists.
Notice that the rules are settings on the branch, not promises in a PR description.
clips.after: fcp's main uses a ruleset with the same ideas, and the independent-approval and locked-checks checks are on its required list.

clips.title: Introducing repository rules
clips.why: GitHub's own short introduction to rulesets, the newer way to write branch rules, and who may bypass them.
look: Rulesets can stack and can be checked in an evaluate mode before they are enforced.
Some actors can be allowed to bypass a ruleset.
clips.after: Our agents' GitHub App is never on the bypass list, so the agent cannot merge even if it is talked into trying.

practice.q: Which command gives the ready gate exactly the CI facts it needs about PR #2512?

options.why: Only the required checks, each with a simple bucket the code can compare.
That lists every check, including ones the rules do not require, as text meant for people.
The body holds the agent's claims, not CI's results.

practice.q: Finish the filter so that only clean buckets pass.
practice.hint: The bucket for a workflow that decided not to run.
practice.why: A skipped check is not a problem: the workflow chose not to run. Everything else that is not pass, including pending, blocks.

practice.q: Put the life of PR #2512 in order.
items: The broker opens the PR as a draft, with Requested-by: @sean as the last line
CI runs on the draft while nobody is pinged
The ready gate reads the required checks, QA results and findings, and finds them clean
The broker sends markPullRequestReadyForReview with the PR's node ID
The reviewer team is asked, Sean gets a Slack message, and the ticket goes back to him
Dana approves, and a person merges
practice.why: Nobody is disturbed until the facts are clean, and the agent's part ends at ready: approving and merging are people's work.

practice.q: Write the last line of the PR body for a ticket Sean asked for.
practice.hint: Two words joined by a hyphen, a colon, then the GitHub login.
practice.why: The approval check reads this line to know who must not approve. Without it, the check fails closed.

practice.q: The gate sees independent-approval / check with bucket fail on a draft. What is right?

options.text: Block: a failing required check always blocks
options.why: This one cannot pass before a person approves, and nobody approves a draft, so blocking on it would keep every PR a draft forever.

options.text: Ignore that check by name, because it waits for the review that ready will start
options.why: It is the only required check that depends on people. Everything else must be clean.

options.text: Approve the PR as the agent so the check passes
options.why: The agent never approves, and its GitHub App has no permission to.
